items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: And Norman Granz, you know the impresario, went down and got him out and he’s the one that got him out.

ctx.x: Now you talked about Lester saying he never felt that he never really made it big because I don’t think he would have said that because of any lack in the power of his playing because he knew he had imitators, he knew that a lot of people were trying to play like him. But once again here we are at an issue where the musician is not receiving the diagnostic thing back that he needs. Other musicians will come up to him and say, “oh man I love the way you play,” but he wasn’t getting the feedback that he needed in…

Well I don’t know. I don’t have too many, I don’t have too many gripes really. I’m kind of satisfied with the way I’ve done. Because see when I got my, after I got my, when I organized my band, I was the leader and I paid the salaries. You know for 21 years I was on the job, you know, one job. So I kind of made it up there. But Prez used to say, he would refer to people, they wasn’t no failure or anything but he acted like it. He referred, he says, “I don’t know,” he says, “all the ladies say they try to play…

making all the money.” He says, “I’m not making any money.” So and he says, “sometimes I don’t know if they’re playing like me or I’m playing like them.” You know he said kind of things like that, you know? So he really didn’t make too much money because he was you know everybody was trying to stay out of the Army and a lot of musicians beat it because it was a lot of jobs and things then, you know with everybody going in, and the musicians just wasn’t Army material, you know. So I remember one time we were out…

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. In the barracks. And they were going to kill him because he said he couldn't get no air. He said he had a little light -- he said he would have died in there. Norman went down there and raised hell and says, "You all don't know what you're doing. You got to let this man out of here."

And they said Norman came on so strong, some of them told him, says, "Well, now, we'll put you in there." And Norman says, "Yeah, but you put me in there, you'll hear from a lot of millionaires and a lot of people," he said, "he ain't got no 'millionaires' , but I --" said, "If you put me in there, I know you all taxis, , but you're going to hear from a lot of big people."
